questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice for the following sentence: 'The teacher is explaining the grammar rules to the students.'
options: The grammar rules were being explained to the students by the teacher.
The grammar rules are explained to the students by the teacher.
The grammar rules are being explained to the students by the teacher.
The grammar rules have been explained to the students by the teacher.
questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the Present Continuous tense ('is explaining'). In passive voice, the continuous aspect is retained using 'being' + past participle ('are being explained').
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Match the idioms in Column I with their correct meanings in Column II:
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' means rarely (III); 'Burn the midnight oil' means work late (II); 'A blessing in disguise' means a hidden benefit (IV); 'Spill the beans' means reveal a secret (I).
columnII: (II) Work or study late into the night
(IV) A good thing that seemed bad at first

questions.question: Directions: Given below are Assertion [As] and Reason [R]. Choose the correct option:
options: Both [As] and [R] are true, and [R] is the correct explanation of [As].
Both [As] and [R] are true, but [R] is not the correct explanation of [As].
questions.explanation: Assertion is correct because 'furniture' is uncountable. Reason correctly explains why uncountable nouns like furniture, information, and scenery do not have plural forms.
questions.assertion: The noun 'furniture' is an uncountable noun and does not take a plural form like 'furnitures'.
questions.reason: Uncountable nouns represent substances, concepts, or categories that cannot be counted individually and lack plural inflections.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Subject-Verb Agreement and select the correct option:
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is incorrect because collective nouns take a singular verb when acting as a single unit (e.g., 'The committee has decided'). Statements 1, 2, and 4 are standard rules of subject-verb agreement.
statements: Two or more singular nouns connected by 'and' usually take a plural verb.
When two subjects are joined by 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it.
Collective nouns always take plural verbs regardless of whether they act as a single unit.
Titles of books or movies, though plural in form, take a singular verb.

questions.question: Identify the one-word substitution for: 'A person who knows everything or has infinite knowledge.'
questions.explanation: 'Omniscient' means knowing everything (derived from 'omni' meaning all + 'scient' meaning knowing). Omnipotent means all-powerful; omnipresent means present everywhere; optimist looks at the brighter side.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences (P, Q, R, S) to form a meaningful paragraph:
questions.explanation: Sentence P starts with 'Reading books...', followed by Q ('but also enriches...') completing the correlative structure 'not only... but also'. Then R introduces the contrast ('In today's digital age...') followed by S ('the habit of reading... is declining'). Thus, P → Q → R → S is correct.
statements: P: Reading books not only broadens our horizons
Q: but also enriches our vocabulary and intellect.
R: In today's digital age, however,
S: the habit of reading printed books is steadily declining.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Match the Direct Speech items in Column I with their correct Indirect Speech forms in Column II:
questions.explanation: 'today' changes to 'that day' and present continuous changes to past continuous (a-II); present perfect changes to past perfect (b-IV); direct question becomes an interrogative indirect clause (c-I); imperative sentence uses 'ordered/told' with infinitive (d-III).
columnI: (a) He said, 'I am going to Patna today.'
(b) She said, 'I have completed my work.'
columnII: (I) Rahul asked where I was going.
(II) He said that he was going to Patna that day.
(III) The teacher ordered the boys to stand up.
(IV) She said that she had completed her work.

questions.question: Choose the correct antonym for the word 'METICULOUS'.
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. Its antonym is 'sloppy' or careless. Careful, punctual, and detailed are synonyms or related words.

questions.question: Directions: Given below are Assertion [As] and Reason [R]. Choose the correct option:
options: Both [As] and [R] are true, and [R] is the correct explanation of [As].
Both [As] and [R] are true, but [R] is not the correct explanation of [As].
questions.explanation: Both assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly justifies why 'is' is singular with 'Neither of the answers'.
questions.assertion: In the sentence 'Neither of the answers is correct', the verb 'is' is correctly used in the singular.
questions.reason: Pronouns like 'each', 'either', and 'neither' are singular and invariably take singular verbs when acting as subjects.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error in the following sentence: 'Hardly had I stepped out of the house (A) / than it started raining heavily (B) / causing severe traffic snarls across the city. (C) / No error (D)'
questions.explanation: The error lies in segment (B). The correlative conjunction for 'Hardly / Scarcely' is 'when' or 'before', not 'than'. 'Than' is used with 'No sooner'.
